subject: prl_ewa or pst_lossgain_q for probabilistic learning task

messages.author: e8e2387233c35cd4
messages.subject: prl_ewa or pst_lossgain_q for probabilistic learning task
parts:
Dear Nate and Young,

I once again would like to request your help, please.

I am using a probabilistic learning task, with three conditions reward, punishment and neutral, as described here (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31201476/). The conditions are intermixed, and have probabilistic associations of 80-20, leading to the optimal outcome. There are 30stimuli per condition.

I would like to model learning rate for negative outcomes/punishment and positive outcomes/reward, and beta. Therefore I selected the prl_ewa and the pst_lossgain_q model.

The prl_ewa is the model for the reversal learning task, I have tried to apply the model to the conditions separately, which I would believe fits the setup of the original Ouden task. However the model fit is extremely bad, with lots of variability in the parameters. Is the model simply not appropriate for the setup of our probabilistic learning task? 

I have also tried the pst_lossgain_q. Here I have modelled all conditions together, marking them as different types (but with the same probabilities) matching it to the original Frank task.

Again the fit is extremely bad:

Would you have any advice on whether it is at all possible to use these models for our task? If so, is there something I can do, like changing the prior?

Thank you very much.
Franziska

messages.author: 4bcf82a01cf98f56
messages.subject: Re: prl_ewa or pst_lossgain_q for probabilistic learning task
parts:
Hi Franziska,

How's rhat of the parameters? I guess pretty bad (> 1.1)? It's hard to tell if convergence was bad from the traceplots.

I haven't checked the paper carefully but is it a reversal learning task? If not, you can just try a simpler model like "bandit2arm_delta"?

Best,
Young
